mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) relative to the prior month's level predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce discount rates applied to equity cash flows during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods with FEDFUNDS declines (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.5 percentage points above 5.5% predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as rising joblessness signals economic deterioration that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC falls below -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 5.0%) and a federal funds rate increase (FEDFUNDS rise > 0.25% month-over-month) predict negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as aggressive monetary tightening to combat inflation compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in periods meeting both conditions (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC falls below -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In early expansion phases, housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1,500,000 units annually (HOUST > 1500) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as robust residential construction signals broad-based economic recovery that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in early expansion phases when HOUST > 1500 (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A positive month-over-month change in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as stronger labor market conditions directly increase consumer spending and corporate revenue growth expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods with PAYEMS growth (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98.0 (index) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as falling manufacturing output signals weakening economic activity that reduces corporate earnings visibility.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC falls below -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1 annualized > 2.0%) combined with weak industrial production (INDPRO < 98.0) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as divergent economic signals indicate an unsustainable expansion that triggers market corrections.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in periods meeting both conditions (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC falls below -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 5.0%), a stable federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS change < 0.1% month-over-month) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as the Fed's restraint avoids sharp market corrections while allowing economic growth to continue.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in high inflation regimes when FEDFUNDS change < 0.1% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
